examples.question_text:
(a) A plant is $137$ cm tall at the end of Month $1$ and grows $3.5$ cm each month. Find its height at the end of Month $8$.
(b) A machine is worth $\$15700$ when bought, at time $0$, and loses $\$850$ in value each year. Find its value after $6$ years.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Month $1$ is the first term, so there are $7$ increases.
$\begin{align*}a_8&=137+(8-1)(3.5)\\&=137+24.5\\&=161.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
(b) The purchase is at time $0$, so there are $6$ decreases.
$\begin{align*}A_6&=15700+6(-850)\\&=15700-5100\\&=\$10600\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
An auditorium has $23$ seats in Row $1$ and $4$ more in each following row.
(a) How many seats are in Row $14$?
(b) What is the total number of seats in the first $14$ rows?
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}a_{14}&=23+(14-1)(4)\\&=75\text{ seats}\end{align*}$
(b) Add all $14$ rows, not just the last row.
$\begin{align*}S_{14}&=\frac{14}{2}(23+75)\\&=7(98)\\&=686\text{ seats}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
(a) A gym member lifts $41.5$ kg in Week $1$ and adds $2.75$ kg each week. In which week does she first lift at least $69$ kg?
(b) A tank has $920$ L on Day $1$ and loses $38$ L each day. On which day does the amount first fall below $570$ L?
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}41.5+(n-1)(2.75)&\ge69\\2.75(n-1)&\ge27.5\\n-1&\ge10\\n&\ge11\end{align*}$
Week $10$: $66.25$ kg; Week $11$: $69$ kg.
The first week is **Week 11**; reaching $69$ kg exactly is allowed by “at least”.
(b)
$\begin{align*}920+(n-1)(-38)&<570\\-38(n-1)&<-350\\n-1&>\frac{350}{38}\\n&>10.2105\ldots\end{align*}$
The least integer is $n=11$.
Day $10$: $578$ L; Day $11$: $540$ L.
The first day is **Day 11**.

examples.question_text: A display has $16$ items in Row $1$, $21$ in Row $2$ and $5$ more in each following row. Row $n$ has $86$ items. Find $n$.
A student saves $\$31$ in Week $1$ and adds $\$2$ to each following weekly deposit. After how many weeks do the deposits total $\$504$?
examples.solution_text:
$a=31$, $d=2$, $S_n=504$.
$\begin{align*}504&=\frac n2[2(31)+(n-1)(2)]\\504&=n(n+30)\\n^2+30n-504&=0\\(n-12)(n+42)&=0\end{align*}$
$n=12$ or $n=-42$.
Reject the negative root: the number of weeks is positive.
The total is reached after **12 weeks**.
Check: $a_{12}=31+11(2)=53$ and $S_{12}=6(31+53)=504$.

examples.derivation: Month 8 follows seven increases: 137+7(3.5)=161.5 cm. Six years after purchase involves six decreases: 15700-6(850)=10600 dollars. The source supports first-period indexing and an initial principal followed by annual changes.
Row 14 contains 23+13(4)=75 seats. The first 14 rows contain 14(23+75)/2=686 seats. These use the supplied nth-term and endpoint-sum formulas.

41.5+2.75(n-1)>=69 gives n>=11; Weeks 10 and 11 have 66.25 and 69 kg. 920-38(n-1)<570 gives n>10.210526...; Days 10 and 11 have 578 and 540 L. Both first admissible indices are 11, with the inclusive and strict thresholds correctly distinguished.
The common difference is 21-16=5. Solving 86=16+5(n-1) gives n-1=14 and n=15, matching the source's specified-term index method.
S_n=n[62+2(n-1)]/2=n(n+30). Setting this equal to 504 gives (n-12)(n+42)=0. Only n=12 is a positive week count. The twelfth deposit is 53 dollars, and 12(31+53)/2=504 dollars.
Six annual salaries total 6[2(47300)+5(1900)]/2=3(104100)=312300 dollars, following the supplied salary-series exercise.
